name: Scroll Network token inflated router balance

classification.summary: The unverified SCROLL token's transfer accounting credited the sending contract with a hugely inflated balance when one wei was routed to the token deployer, so a UniversalRouter TRANSFER command left the router holding more than a thousand times the Uniswap V2 pair's SCROLL reserve, which the attacker then pushed into the pair and swapped out for WETH.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/scroll-network-token.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.

sources.note: onchain review: SCROLL 'Scroll Network' 0xe51D3dE9b81916D383eF97855C271250852eC7B7 created 2024-05-26T19:30:11Z by 0x72c509b05a44c4bb53373efc2e76fb75fa8108a6, not the attack-tx sender 0x55db954f0121e09ec838a20c216eabf35ca32cdd; no EIP-1967 events, unverified source, so age runs from deployment (2.16 days). Verified at block 19971610 that UniversalRouter 0x3fC91A3afd70395Cd496C647d5a6CC9D4B2b7FAD held 0 SCROLL and the WETH pair held 1.363e23, confirming the router's balance was created by the exploit's first TRANSFER rather than pre-existing. ~76 ETH at a May 2024 ETH price near $3,800 is roughly $290k. Loss converted at the incident timestamp: 76 ETH x $3,849.77 (DefiLlama historical ETH price) = $292,583.

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/scroll-network-token.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
The legacy USD loss lacks uniformly structured valuation provenance.
